21:2: If you buy a Hebrew slave who is a son of a Hebrew,
he shall serve [you] for six years,
but in the seventh [year] he is to go out free, for naught [without liability].
21:6: His master must bring him before the judges.
He must then bring him next to the door,
and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl.
He will be a working servant for him, forever.
21:8: If she is displeasing to her master, for otherwise he would have designated her as his wife, he must allow her to be redeemed.
He has no power [right] to sell her to another man for he has controlled her.
21:9: If he has designated her as a wife for his son,
he must grant her exactly the same rights as daughters of Yisrael.
21:13: But if he did not lie in wait [to ambush him]
but from before God he was brought to his hand,
then I will designate for you a place,
to which he can flee [and find refuge].
21:16: Whoever steals [kidnaps] a person from B’nei Yisrael and sells him, if he is found in his hand, he shall be put to death.
21:18: and one man hits his fellow
with a stone or with [his] fist;
and he [the victim] does not die but falls to idleness,
21:19: If he gets up and is able to walk on the outside on his own power, the one who struck him shall be acquitted.
Still he must pay for his loss of work, and must pay the doctor’s fee.
21:20: If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod,
and [the slave] dies under his hand,
21:21: However if he [the slave] survives for a day or two,
for he [the slave] is his [master’s] property.
21:25: [Compensation of] a burn for a burn,
21:31: Whether it is a son [a minor lad] of Yisrael that the ox gores or a daughter [a minor girl] of Yisrael that it gored,
this law shall apply to it.
21:32: If the ox gored a male or female slave,
he must give thirty silver selaim to their master,
and the ox must be stoned.
22:2: If eyes of witnesses fell upon him, there is liability for his blood.
If he does not have [the means to do so],
he shall be sold [as a slave to pay] for his theft.
22:3: If the stolen article is found in his hand [possession], whether it is an ox, donkey or sheep that is alive,
he must pay two live animals.
22:7: If the thief is not found,
the owner of the house [the watchman] must come before the judges [Beis Din],
[to swear] that he did not lay a hand on that which his neighbor handed over to him.
22:8: In every question of dishonesty whether it involves an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything that was [allegedly] lost of which [a witness] says, “This is it!”
the claims of both parties must be brought before the judges.
The one whom the judges find guilty,
must pay double restitution to his neighbor.
22:10: an oath to Adonoy shall be between them,
that he [the watcher] did not lay his hand on that which his neighbor handed over to him.
The owner must accept it [the oath], and [the watcher] need not make restitution.
22:12: If it was torn apart [killed by wild beasts], he [the watcher] must provide witnesses that it was torn apart.
He then need not pay for that which was torn apart.
22:15: If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her;
he must establish her as his wife.
22:19: Whoever slaughters to false gods of the peoples must be condemned [to die].
[Sacrifices may be offered] to the Name of Adonoy alone.
22:24: When you lend money to My people, to the poor person who is with [among] you,
do not act toward him as a [demanding] creditor.
Do not place an injury upon him.
22:26: For this alone is his covering,
With what shall he lie down [to sleep]?
If it happens that he cries out before Me,
I will accept [his cry] for I am gracious.
22:28: [Your offering of] the fullness [of your newly ripened produce] and of your terumah-offering’s you must not delay.
The first-born of your sons, you shall separate before Me.
22:29: You must do likewise with your oxen and with your sheep.
Seven days it shall remain with its mother.
On the eighth day you must separate it before Me.
22:30: You shall be men of holiness before Me,
and you must not eat flesh that was torn off from a living animal.
23:1: Do not accept a false report.
Do not join hands with a wicked man to be for him
23:2: Do not follow the majority to do evil.
Do not refrain from teaching what is proper in your eyes regarding a judgment. It must be decided by the majority.
23:3: Do not show favor [even] to the poor in his judgment.
23:5: If you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden,
and you might stop yourself from abandoning him,
[you should] abandon what is in your heart against him and unload with him.
23:7: Keep far away from anything false.
Do not kill one who is innocent or one who goes out innocent from judgment,
for I will not acquit a wicked person.
23:8: for bribery blinds the eyes of the wise,
and perverts the words of justice.
23:13: Preserve everything that I have said to you.
Do not mention the name of false gods of the peoples.
You must not cause it to be heard through your mouth.
23:15: You must keep the festival of Matzos.
You must eat matzos for seven days, as I have commanded you. [This festival must be celebrated] at the appointed time, during the month when the grain is ripened,
for in it [at this time] you went out of Egypt.
23:17: every male among you must appear
before the Master of the world, Adonoy.
23:18: You must not sacrifice — while chometz is present — My [Pesach] sacrifice.
You must not allow to remain overnight off the Altar — the fats of the festival-offering — until morning.
23:19: The beginning of the first fruits of your land
must be brought to the Sanctuary of Adonoy, your God.
You must not eat meat with milk.
23:21: Be careful in his presence and heed [obey] his word. Do not rebel against him;
for he cannot bear [pardon] your transgression,
for His word is in My Name.
23:22: But if you truly listen to [obey] his word,
and do all that I speak,
then I will be an enemy to your enemies,
and attack those who attack you.
23:24: You must not prostrate yourself to their false gods, nor serve [sacrifice to] them.
You must not adopt their customs.
and completely break down their monuments.
23:25: You must serve before Adonoy, your God,
and He will bless your food and your drink.
I will eliminate bad sickness from your midst.
23:27: I will send My dread ahead of you,
and I will bring panic to all the people
among whom you will come to fight against.
I will make all your enemies turn their backs before you.
23:32: Do not make a pact with them or with their false gods.
23:33: Do not allow them to live in your land,
since they may cause you to sin before Me;
and this would be a [fatal] trap to you.
24:1: He [God] had said to Moshe, ‘Go up before Adonoy, you, Aharon, Nadav, Avihu,
and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael,
and prostrate yourselves at a distance.
24:2: and the people must not go up with him.”
24:4: Moshe wrote down all the words of Adonoy.
He arose early in the morning,
and built an altar at the foot of the mountain,
for the twelve tribes of [the B’nei] Yisrael.
24:5: He sent the youths [first-born] of B’nei Yisrael
and sacrificed oxen as peace-offerings before Adonoy.
24:7: He then took the Book of the Covenant,
They said, “All that Adonoy has spoken, we will do and we will obey.”
24:8: and cast it on the Altar to atone on behalf of the people,
and he said, “Behold, this is the blood of the covenant which Adonoy has made with you
24:10: They saw [a vision of] the Glory of the God of Yisrael,
and under the throne of His Glory [there was something] like a brickwork of precious stone,
and it was like the image of heaven in purity.
24:11: But against the nobility of the B’nei Yisrael,
and they rejoiced in their sacrifices which were accepted graciously as if they ate and drank.
24:12: Adonoy then said to Moshe, “Come up before Me to the mountain and remain there.
I will give you the tablets of stone, the Torah and the commandment,
which I have written [in order] to teach them.”
24:13: Moshe and Yehoshua, his attendant, set out,
but [only] Moshe went up to the mountain upon which the Glory of God was revealed.
24:14: He [Moshe] said to the elders, “Wait here for us
and Aharon and Chur will be with you.
Whoever has a claim can approach before them.”
24:17: The appearance of Adonoy’s glory was like
the appearance of a consuming flame at the top to the mountain;
before the eyes of the B’nei Yisrael.
